summary:
Verified from the supplied page text and inlined keys, without running code:
• The diagonal Gaussian product identity, added precisions, precision-weighted mean, covariance formula, and normalizer Z = N(μa; μb, Σa + Σb) are correct.
• Setting (b) correctly gives mean 0, product sd 0.070710678, distance 10 expert standard deviations, and log Z −1583.406832.
• Setting (a) correctly gives head mean +0.980198020, body mean −0.980198020, and log Z −46.465787.
• Making the dog head sure correctly gives head mean 0, body mean −0.980198020, and log Z −814.936310.
• Setting (c) has the stated component means. Its unnormalized log weights −24.089706 and −803.213808, and their gap 779.124102, are correct. The side-by-side components dominate, subject to the exact-weight correction below.
• At ᾱ = 0.5, the noised head variances 0.505 and 1, precision ratio 1.980198, fixed-level product mean +0.232570, and noised-clean-product mean +0.693105 are correct. Their displayed difference rounds to 0.461.
• The press 10 exercise correctly gives head mean 48/52 = 0.923076923 when the variances are 0.02 and 0.5.
• The supplied printout reproduces all 18 walk-key numbers and reports coverage of 2401 variance states and 247 noise states. Those execution claims were not independently rerun.

review_findings.where: [Errors] Press 1: Sure everywhere: a grey blend
review_findings.finding: “Each pixel's product is 0” confuses a distribution with its mean. The product is a nondegenerate Gaussian with mean 0 and sd 0.070710678, so the pixel itself is not identically 0. The supplied key's positive sd proves this.
review_findings.suggested_text: Each pixel's product distribution has mean 0 and sd 0.071. Its mean is 10 of each expert's standard deviations from that expert's mean.

review_findings.where: [Errors] Press 4: Make the dog's head sure
review_findings.finding: “Nearer 0 is more overlap” is not true of log Z in general. Z is a Gaussian product normalizer, not an overlap coefficient bounded by 1. For two identical N(0, 0.01) experts, Z = (2π × 0.02)⁻¹ᐟ² > 1 and log Z > 0, with log Z tending to +∞ as their common variance tends to 0 (by hand). The claimed ordering is valid only for the particular fixed opposite-mean comparisons being shown.
review_findings.suggested_text: log Z is the log normalizer of the product. For the fixed +1 versus −1 comparisons on this page, a less negative log Z means greater compatibility. This ordering is not a general rule for arbitrary means and variances.

review_findings.finding: “8 × (−99.0) + 8 × (−2.9) = −814.9” is false with the displayed rounded operands. They give −815.2 (by hand). The stated −814.9 is obtained only from the unrounded terms −98.962927 and −2.904112.
review_findings.suggested_text: Using the unrounded per-pixel values, 8 × (−98.962927) + 8 × (−2.904112) = −814.936, which rounds to −814.9.

review_findings.where: [Errors] Press 7: Clashing pairs lose their weight
review_findings.finding: “so it takes all the weight,” together with “w 0” for same-half pairs and “0.50” under “THE FOUR PAIRS EXACT,” turns numerical underflow and rounding into exact mathematics. Every prior and Gaussian overlap is positive, so all four normalized weights are strictly positive. With r = e⁻⁷⁷⁹·¹²⁴, each side-by-side weight is 1/[2(1+r)] and each same-half weight is r/[2(1+r)].
review_findings.suggested_text: The two side-by-side pairs take essentially all the weight. With r = e⁻⁷⁷⁹·¹²⁴, each side-by-side pair has weight 1/[2(1+r)] and each same-half pair has weight r/[2(1+r)]. These values print as 0.50 and 0 at the displayed precision, but they are not exactly 0.5 and 0.

review_findings.where: [Errors] Press 8: Noise both experts halfway, repeated in Press 9 and Disclosure
review_findings.finding: “adding the two experts' scores at each noise level, which samples the product of the noised experts” overstates what the calculation establishes. At a fixed ᾱ, the score sum is indeed the score of the density proportional to the two noised densities' product. That family need not be the marginal family of a valid reverse diffusion, so the fixed-level mean does not determine what a full reverse run samples. In the full-noise limit, each expert is N(0, 1), their product is proportional to N(0, 1/2), and the forward-noised clean product is N(0, 1) (by hand), which already shows that the two time-indexed families differ.
review_findings.suggested_text: At this fixed noise level, adding the two scores gives the score of qᾱ(x) ∝ pcat,ᾱ(x) pdog,ᾱ(x). For these Gaussian factors, qᾱ has head mean +0.233 at ᾱ = 0.5. This fixed-level calculation does not by itself determine the distribution generated by a full reverse run.

review_findings.finding: The displayed rounded values are used in exact equalities: “16 × (−1.419) = −22.703” and “8 × (−98.963) + 8 × (−1.266) = −801.828.” The displayed operands instead give −22.704 and −801.832 respectively (by hand). The reported totals are correct when the unrounded per-pixel values are used.
review_findings.suggested_text: Each pair starts at log 0.25 ≈ −1.386. Using unrounded per-pixel log overlaps, a side-by-side pair adds −22.703, giving −24.090 after the prior. A same-half pair adds −801.828, giving −803.214 after the prior.

review_findings.where: [Missing steps] Press 5: Sure clashes cost overlap
review_findings.finding: “A sure +1 against a sure −1 adds −99.0 to log Z per pixel; sure against loose adds −2.9” presents the crucial costs without substituting into the stated Gaussian normalizer. The proposed insertion supplies the missing evaluation and the aggregation over eight head and eight body pixels. The substitutions are computed by hand.
review_findings.suggested_text:
Head: log Zhead = log N(+1; −1, 0.01 + 0.01).
Rule: the Gaussian product normalizer is N(μa; μb, va + vb).
log Zhead = −½[log(2π × 0.02) + 4/0.02] = −98.963.
Rule: use the one-dimensional Gaussian log density.
Body: log Zbody = log N(+1; −1, 1 + 0.01).
Rule: the Gaussian product normalizer is N(μa; μb, va + vb).
log Zbody = −½[log(2π × 1.01) + 4/1.01] = −2.904.
Rule: use the one-dimensional Gaussian log density.
log Ztotal = 8 log Zhead + 8 log Zbody = −814.936 ≈ −814.9.
Rule: independent pixel normalizers multiply, so their logs add.

review_findings.where: [Missing steps] Press 7: Clashing pairs lose their weight
review_findings.finding: The page jumps from the two unnormalized log weights to normalized weights 0 and 0.50 without displaying the normalization. That omitted step is also where one sees that the printed zeros are only numerical approximations.
review_findings.suggested_text:
Let H = −24.089706 and L = −803.213808.
Rule: H and L are the high and low unnormalized log weights, each occurring twice.
Δ = H − L = 779.124102.
Rule: subtract log weights to obtain the log weight ratio.
r = exp(L − H) = exp(−Δ).
Rule: exponentiate the log ratio.
D = 2 exp(H) + 2 exp(L) = 2 exp(H)(1+r).
Rule: sum the four unnormalized weights.
wside = exp(H)/D = 1/[2(1+r)].
Rule: divide an unnormalized weight by D.
wsame = exp(L)/D = r/[2(1+r)].
Rule: divide an unnormalized weight by D.

review_findings.where: [Simplifications] Press 3: Each pixel follows the surer expert
review_findings.finding: The current route says “A head pixel weighs the cat's 100 against the dog's 1” and then expands the precision-weighted formula. With fixed means +1 and −1, the expression simplifies directly: [(+1)/vcat + (−1)/vdog]/[1/vcat + 1/vdog] = (vdog − vcat)/(vdog + vcat). This makes every variance-slider result easier to read.
review_findings.suggested_text: For cat mean +1 and dog mean −1, product mean = (vdog − vcat)/(vdog + vcat). On the head this is (1 − 0.01)/(1 + 0.01) = 99/101 = +0.980. Swapping the variances on the body changes only the sign, giving −0.980.

review_findings.where: [Notation clashes] Press 6: Let each animal pick a side, continued in Press 7
review_findings.finding: The grid defines “w: the pair's weight in the product,” so w is normalized, but labels −24.1 and −803.2 as “log w.” Those values are unnormalized log weights. They cannot be logarithms of the neighboring normalized values 0.50 and 0. The Disclosure likewise uses wij for a normalized quantity defined only up to proportionality, then informally calls the unnormalized value log w.
review_findings.suggested_text:
Use w for normalized pair weight and ℓ for unnormalized log pair weight.
ℓij = log πi + log ρj + log N(μi; νj, Σi + Λj).
wij = exp(ℓij) / Σkl exp(ℓkl).
In the grid, replace “log w” with “ℓ, unnormalized log weight”.
